title: Operational Resilience: Scenario Library, Runbooks, and Customer Communication Kits
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary
This page is a consolidated, actionable reference for operational resilience: a scenario library (high-level triage + dedicated runbooks), game-day / exercise plans, on-call rotation guidance, and ready-made customer and status-page communication kits. It is intended for first responders, on-call SREs, incident commanders, product on-call engineers, and customer success teams.

Goals
- Reduce time-to-diagnosis for common classes of incidents (latency spikes, model degradation, capacity exhaustion, auth/ingress failures).
- Standardize communications to customers and internal stakeholders.
- Provide measurable exercise templates for improving SLO attainment and runbook coverage.

How to use this page
1) Read the severity matrix below to classify incidents.
2) Follow the scenario checklist for the matching incident class.
3) Escalate to the runbook owner and apply runbook steps.
4) Use the communication templates verbatim (edit only the bracketed fields).
5) After resolution, run the postmortem checklist and schedule a blameless review within 72 hours.

Incident severity matrix (quick reference)
- SEV-0 (Platform outage): Service unavailable across multiple regions or core API returns >50% 5xx across customers for >5 minutes.
- SEV-1 (Major degradation): Latency >2x P99 target or error rate >5% for production endpoints impacting multiple customers for >15 minutes.
- SEV-2 (Partial impact): Single-customer outage, queued requests, or feature regressions reducing throughput or model quality for a subset of traffic.
- SEV-3 (Minor): Nonblocking bugs, dashboard/metrics gaps, or cosmetic UI issues.

SLOs and alerting thresholds (examples we enforce)
| SLO | Goal | Alert threshold | Pager escalation |
|-----|------|----------------|-----------------|
| API availability (global) | 99.95% monthly | Incident if 5xx rate >20% for 5 minutes | SEV-0 |
| P99 latency (text-generation) | <1200ms | Alert if P99 >2500ms for 10 minutes | SEV-1 |
| Embedding throughput (dedicated pool) | 95% of committed capacity | Alert if queued >30% for 15 min | SEV-1 |

Scenario library (selection of high-value scenarios)
1) Large-scale latency spike (multi-region)
- Typical cause: kernel regression, autoscaler misconfiguration, cold caches, network flapping.
- Initial triage checklist:
  1. Confirm alert: check /metrics/api/5xx_rate and /metrics/latency/p99 across regions.
  2. Identify scope: run `curl -sS https://ops-api.internal/telemetry?range=15m` or open Grafana dashboard "API-Latency-Overview".
  3. Check recent deploys: `git log -n 5 --pretty=format:"%h %s" --deploy-tag` and the rollout dashboard.
  4. Verify cache hit rates: /metrics/cache/prefix_hit_rate.
  5. If CPU/GPU throttling present, check node metrics: `kubectl top pods -n runtime` and `nvidia-smi` on affected hosts.
- Primary runbook: eng-serving-runtime/diagnose-latency-spike (owner: runtime oncall).
- Quick mitigations (apply while diagnosing):
  - Temporarily reduce batch size to limit tail latency: `PATCH /internal/configuration` body `{\"batch_size\": 1}` (apply to affected model pool).
  - Increase autoscaler target min replicas for the pool: `infractl autoscale set --pool <pool-id> --min 4`.
  - Failover traffic to standby region following the smart routing playbook (see below).

2) Capacity exhaustion on Dedicated pools
- Typical cause: unexpected customer load, quota misreporting, autoscaler failure.
- Initial triage checklist:
  1. Check pool utilization: Grafana "Dedicated-Pool-Utilization" and `infractl pool describe <pool-id>`.
  2. Confirm quota accounting: `billing-api /pools/<id>/usage`.
  3. Identify heavy tenants with `kafka audit` and `tenant-usage-service` query.
- Primary runbook: eng-sre/dedicated-pool-backpressure-and-eviction (owner: infra).
- Quick mitigations:
  - Enable backpressure for non-critical routes: `policyctl set backpressure --routes pattern=embeddings:* --level moderate`.
  - Activate defined bursts if available: `infractl bursts enable --pool <pool-id> --duration 10m`.
  - Notify on-call CS rep to check if affected customer has emergency burst credit.

3) Authentication / onboarding ingress failures
- Typical cause: KMS outage, mis-rotated keys, proxy misconfig.
- Triage checklist:
  1. Verify KMS status and keyring: `aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <key>` or HSM dashboard.
  2. Check gateway logs: `kubectl logs gateway-0 -n ingress | grep AuthService`.
  3. Validate token issuance: `authz-cli validate --token <sample-token>`.
- Primary runbook: security-and-compliance/authz-failure-playbook (owner: security).

Runbook structure (standardized)
- Title (clear): short phrase + owner team
- Symptoms: bullet list
- Impact: how to determine scope / SLO hit
- Preconditions: required ACLs, diagnostic tools, runbook prerequisites
- Step-by-step remediation (numbered) with commands and rollback guidance
- Post-resolution actions: tickets, customer notifications, follow-up tasks
- When to escalate: explicit signals (e.g., >10% traffic loss after 15m)

Runbook example excerpt: diagnose-service-degradation (short form)
1) Confirm the incident and set a bridge: `incidentctl create --severity SEV-1 --summary \"P99 >2500ms for text-generation\"`
2) Assign roles: Incident Commander (IC), Lead Triage Engineer, Communication Lead, Exec Liaison.
3) Collect evidence: attach trace IDs, request samples, and Grafana links to the incident.
4) Attempt a safe rollback of the last model-serving release: `deployctl rollback --service runtime --to-tag <previous>` (ensure canary traffic is healthy first).
5) If rollback not possible, apply throttling policy: `policyctl throttle --route /v1/generate --percent 50`.
6) Monitor the effect for 5 minutes; document metrics snapshot.

Communication kits (templates)
- Internal Slack (immediate):
  > [INCIDENT] SEV-1: P99 latency for text-generation >2500ms across us-west/us-east. IC: @aisha, Bridge: <bridge-link>. Actions: rollback underway.

- Status page public template (initial):
  Title: Service Degradation: Text Generation Latency
  Impact: Users may experience higher-than-normal response times for text generation.
  Affected products: Redwood API (text generation)
  Start time: [YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC]
  Current status: Investigating
  Next update: in 15 minutes
  Root cause: TBD

- Customer-facing email (short update):
  Subject: Update: Redwood API - degraded text-generation performance

  Hi [Customer Name],

  We are investigating a performance degradation affecting text-generation requests. Our SRE team has identified elevated P99 latency and is executing a rollback and failover plan. We will provide another update within 15 minutes.

  Impact: increased response times; requests are not timing out.
  Actions in progress: rollback of last deploy, targeted traffic routing, and autoscaler adjustments.

  Contact: [customer-success-email] or reply to this thread.

  — Redwood Inference Operations

Customer comms guidance
- Use plain language; avoid root-cause speculation until confirmed.
- Avoid technical dumps in the first 2 updates; provide timeline and mitigation steps instead.
- Escalate to the Customer Success lead for any enterprise customer with SLA exposure or regulatory constraints.

Post-incident process (postmortem checklist)
1) Create a postmortem doc using the template (link: /confluence/templates/postmortem).
2) Fill in timeline (UTC) with evidence and decision points.
3) Tag code/infra changes with PRs and links.
4) Quantify customer impact: number of customers affected, error volume, SLO burn.
5) Define care-plan for any impacted enterprise customers (owner: CS).
6) Assign action items with owners and target dates; include verification criteria.
7) Present summary in weekly FRR (fault review) with the three most important takeaways.

On-call rotation & handoff standards
- Rotation length: 1 week for primary SREs; 2-week swing for platform leads.
- Coverage model: primary, secondary, and overflow (engineering floater).
- Handoff checklist (to be completed in Slack and incident ticket):
  - Current on-call status and pager routes active
  - Ongoing incidents with severity and short status
  - Scheduled maintenance and expected noise windows
  - Key contact details for escalation (CS lead, legal, security, executive liaison)
  - Link to runbook(s) used today and any temporary mitigations applied

Game Day / Exercise curriculum (quarterly recommended)
- Frequency: quarterly mandatory game day for each SRE and runtime engineering pair.
- Example exercise: Region failover simulation
  - Goal: verify smart routing and stateful KV cache replay under failover.
  - Preconditions: synthetic traffic harness enabled, canary tokens, simulated region outage toggled via `infractl region-outage simulate --region us-west1`.
  - Steps: trigger outage, failover traffic, validate request success for 5k synthetic requests, observe cache warmup time, and measure P99.
  - Success criteria: failover completes without >2% additional error rate and less than 3x P99 latency for the first 5 minutes.
- After-action review: publish exercise notes, update related runbooks, and create Jira tickets for any gaps.

Status page update cadence and responsibilities
- When incident declared SEV-1+: update status page within 10 minutes (initial), then every 15 minutes until mitigation, then hourly during remediation, and final update with root cause and postmortem link.
- Owner: Communication Lead (role assigned in incident).

Escalation matrix (condensed)
- SEV-0: IC -> CTO -> Legal & CS -> Exec on-call.
- SEV-1: IC -> Eng Manager (runtime/infra) -> CS lead.
- SEV-2: IC -> Team on-call -> Product PM.
- Escalation triggers: sustained SLO degradation >30 minutes, legal/regulatory exposure, or customer outage with SLA violation.

Operational tooling & useful commands
- incidentctl: create/annotate incident tickets and bridges (`incidentctl create --severity SEV-1 --summary \"...\"`).
- infractl: pool and region controls (`infractl autoscale set`, `infractl pool describe`).
- policyctl: runtime routing and throttling policies.
- deployctl: safe rollbacks and canary controls.
- Example: failover to standby region
  1) `policyctl route set --svc api --to-region us-east1 --weight 100`
  2) Monitor `curl -sS https://ops-api.internal/telemetry?range=5m`
  3) If errors increase, revert `policyctl route set --svc api --to-region us-west1 --weight 100`

Runbook maintenance cadence
- Owners must review runbooks they own every 6 months or after a game-day if exercise exposed gaps.
- Retire or rewrite runbooks with >3 stakeholder-reported failures in a quarter.

Appendix: incident communication templates (copy-and-paste)
- Initial internal incident creation (IC uses this in bridge):
  > Title: [SEV-1] <short summary>
  > Bridge: <bridge-link>
  > IC: @<name>
  > Roles: Triage, CommLead, ExecLiaison
  > Evidence: Grafana links, sample trace IDs

- Final postmortem summary (public-friendly)
  Title: Postmortem: [SEV-1] Text-generation latency spike — [YYYY-MM-DD]
  Summary: Short non-technical summary of what happened, impact, and customer-facing remediation.
  Impact: Affected 12 customers, increase in P99 to 3.2s for 7 minutes; no data loss.
  Root cause: A scheduling regression in kernel selector after traffic shift caused increased tail latency.
  Remediation: Reverted the faulty selection algorithm; added additional unit + integration tests; deployment gating adjusted.
  Action items: list with owners and due dates.

Contacts and ownership (quick directory)
- Incident Commander rotation: sashas@redwood.ai (primary), aisha@redwood.ai (backup)
- Runtime oncall: #runtime-oncall (Slack)
- Infra oncall: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
- CS escalation: cs-leads@redwood.ai

Document history and governance
This page replaces ad-hoc checklists and consolidates communication kits and scenario templates. Owners must keep the page up-to-date and include any new templates derived from customer-facing incidents.

If you find missing scenarios or need an additional runbook added to the library, open a PR on the docs repo and ping @aisha for review.
